data.title: Microvision, Shutterstock among technology stocks to join Russell Microcap; Ouster, Penguin Solutions to exit
data.description:
FTSE Russell has released a preliminary list of companies set to join or leave the Russell Microcap Index as part of its annual reconstitution.

Following telecommunications companies are slated to join the index: Microvision (MVIS), Shutterstock (SSTK), Vulcan Infrastructure (VIP), Kodiak AI (KDK), and Angel Studios (ANGX).

Technology firms leaving the index include Ouster (OUST), Penguin Solutions (PENG), Veritone (VERI), Soluna Holdings (SLNH), and Blaize Holdings (BZAI)

The newly reconstituted indexes take effect after the U.S. market close on Dec. 11.

data.title: Shopify, NXP Semiconductors among technology stocks to join Russell 3000 index; One Stop Systems, Veritone to exit
data.description:
FTSE Russell has released a preliminary list of companies set to join or leave the Russell 3000 Index as part of its 2026 annual reconstitution.
 
The technology companies that are set to join the index include Shopify (SHOP), NXP Semiconductors (NXPI), Firy (FIRY), Netskope (NTSK), and Quantum Corp (QMCO), among others.
 
The telecommunications companies that are slated to leave the index include One Stop Systems (OSS), Veritone (VERI), Atomera (ATOM), Soluna Holdings (SLNH), and Intellicheck (IDN).
 
The newly reconstituted indexes take effect after the U.S. market close on December 11.

data.title: Bitcoin plunges 6%, dips under $58K
data.description:
Bitcoin (BTC-USD) sank more than 5.9% on Friday as Wall Street’s enthusiasm on technology and artificial intelligence fizzled out, accompanying a selloff that dipped the cryptocurrency below $58,000.

Bitcoin (BTC-USD) is down more than 34% year-to-date and down almost 29% this month alone. The crypto has also lost more than 40% from its high point in a year.

Moreover, its decline has followed the tech trade selloff, suffering alongside the Nasdaq, which is down more than 5%, and the S&P 500 (SP500), down more than 3.5%. South Korea’s Kospi index also fell more than 5%.

Within the ETFs, BlackRock’s iShares Bitcoin Trust (IBIT) lost $541.1M on Thursday, marking its biggest one-day outflow on record. Also, other U.S. spot bitcoin ETFs lost about $582M in total.

Bitcoin-backed ETFs: (IBIT), (ARKB), (GBTC), (BRRR), (BTCO), (HODL), (BTCW), (FBTC), (BITB), and (EZBC).

data.title: Business development companies post hit to Q3 NAV on realized, unrealized losses
data.description:
During the third quarter, business development companies faced credit challenges as realized and unrealized losses lowered net asset values, according to a report by Morningstar DBRS.

BDC earnings have not yet benefited from the recent increase in base rates. However, strategic portfolio repositioning efforts improved portfolio diversity, capitalization levels, and lower payment-in-kind interest.

"Liquidity is a top priority for BDCs with elevated redemptions and upcoming debt maturities; however, asset repayments and open, but more expensive, debt capital markets have largely mitigated liquidity risk," said the report.

The credit rating agency said it does not expect significant downward pressure on the credit ratings of BDCs unless there is material deterioration in asset quality coupled with elevated leverage above target ranges.

Here is a look at some BDC credit ratings, as assigned by DBRS:

  • Carlyle Secured Lending (CGBD) - BBB (high)

data.title: Fastenal, Grainger cut at Baird, as outlook for industrial distributors turns negative
data.description:
Fastenal (FAST) and WW Grainger (GWW) fell 2.9% and 3.5%, respectively, in Friday's trading after both stocks were downgraded to Neutral from Outperform at Baird, which said valuation, momentum, and Federal Reserve policy have all turned negative for industrial distributors.

Margins in the sector are near peak levels, price increases are moderating, and Y/Y comparisons are becoming more difficult, Baird analyst David Manthey said, seeing the potential for slower earnings growth and revisions, particularly if AI-related investment moderates and/or the U.S. economy experiences a mid-cycle slowdown.

Manthey said he remains constructive on the longer-term industrial recovery and secular drivers, including reshoring and automation, but believes the near-term risk/reward has deteriorated, so with substantial relative outperformance already captured, elevated expectations, and a less supportive economic and market backdrop, the analyst said he leans more cautious on industrial distributors.

Should AI-related investment moderate and/or the U.S. economy experiences a mid-cycle slowdown, current earnings estimates may prove optimistic, while political uncertainty, including a potential December 11 federal government shutdown, further complicates the outlook, Manthey said.
